texts.li: [lowtech] A courier's satchel, the leather gone black with rain, half sunk in the mud by the old road. {A_nameDef} pulled it out and found a bundle of letters inside, tied with string and sealed with wax, every one, for people in {FACTION}'s country. The top one is for {X_nameDef}, at {PLACE}.\n\nWhoever was carrying them never got there. From the state of the satchel, that was years ago.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} found a mailbag snagged in a thicket below the road, the canvas rotten and the zip rusted shut. Inside are two dozen letters, still sealed, for people in {FACTION}'s towns. The top one is addressed to {X_nameDef} at {PLACE}, in a careful, hopeful hand.\n\nThe postmarks are years old. Whoever was carrying them didn't make it.

[winter] Clearing snow by the old road, {A_nameDef} turned up a courier's satchel frozen into the bank. The letters inside are dry, wrapped in oilcloth, and sealed: two dozen of them, for people in {FACTION}'s country. The one on top is for {X_nameDef}, at {PLACE}.\n\nThey have been lying there for years.

[river] The river gave up a courier's satchel this morning, washed into the reeds below the colony. {A_nameDef} fished it out. The letters inside were wrapped in oilcloth, and most of them are still dry: two dozen, sealed, for people in {FACTION}'s towns. The top one is for {X_nameDef}, at {PLACE}.

li.label: Send them on with the next trader
li.outcome: The satchel goes into a dry box to wait for the next trader bound for {FACTION}'s country. They'll be years late, but they'll get there.

li.label: Read them first
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sits down at the table with a knife for the seals and a lamp, and the colony gathers round to listen.

li.label: Burn them
li.outcome: The letters go into the stove still sealed, and the wax spits as it melts.

coming.li: [lettersreply,sent] The old letters found by the road are on their way to {FACTION}'s country with a trader. If anyone answers, it should be within {DAYS}.
[lettersreply,personal] The old letter to {X_nameDef} is on its way to {PLACE}, with one of {A_nameDef}'s own. An answer may come within {DAYS}.
[letterssecret] {A_nameDef} is reading the old letters found by the road, one by one.
[dug] {A_nameDef} is out with a spade, looking for the place the old letter describes. Back within {DAYS}.
[cashed] The old note of credit is on its way to {PLACE} to be cashed. Word within {DAYS}.

remembered.li: [lost] The old letters reached {FACTION}'s country, or so the trader said. Not one answer has come back.
[lost] The colony sent the old letters off with a trader bound for {FACTION}. No word has come back yet.

endings.li: [thanked,love] {X_nameDef} has gone home to {PLACE} with the letter folded inside {X_possessive} coat, and the colony has had a gift from {X_objective} by way of thanks: {ITEM}.\n\n{A_nameDef} went as far as the road with {X_objective}, and says {X_nameDef} was smiling the whole way.

[thanked,personal] {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} with the old letter and {A_nameDef}'s new one folded inside it, and a gift came for the colony afterward, by way of thanks: {ITEM}.\n\nThey have promised to write to each other.
[thanked] {X_nameDef} is home in {PLACE} again, and has sent the colony something by way of thanks: {ITEM}. {FACTION} have heard the story by now, and like the colony the better for it.

[shared] {X_nameDef} sent half of the family silver up the road to the colony, {ITEM} silver in all, with a note: "Without your letter there'd be none of it."\n\n{FACTION} have heard the story, and think well of the colony.
[repaid] The old note of credit was honored at {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} has sent the colony a share of it: {ITEM} silver. The note had been owed to {X_possessive} family for eleven years.

[joined,love] {X_nameDef} unpacked in the colony's guest room and stayed. The letter is pinned to the wall above the bed. {X_nameDef} says there's nobody waiting at {PLACE} anymore, and the colony has been kind.
[joined] {X_nameDef} came to thank the colony and stayed for good. There's nothing left for {X_objective} at {PLACE}, {X_nameDef} says, and a great deal to do here.

[dug] {A_nameDef} found the spot the letter described, under a lightning-split tree, and dug down until the spade hit iron. The family's silver is the colony's now: {ITEM} silver.\n\nThe letter went into the stove. The family at {PLACE} will never know.
[cashed] The old note of credit was honored at {PLACE}, no questions asked. {ITEM} silver came back with the trader.\n\nThe family it was meant for never saw it.
[burned] The letters burned. A trader at the gate today mentioned a family at {PLACE} who have been waiting years for word from someone who went away. {A_nameDef} didn't say anything.
[burned,read] The letters burned, after the colony had read every one. {A_nameDef} still remembers some of the lines, and wishes {A_pronoun} didn't.
[lost] The letters reached {FACTION}'s country, as far as anyone knows. No answer has come back, and none will now.

summaries.li: [thanked] The colony sent on letters lost for years, and {X_nameDef} came to thank it.
[shared] The colony sent on a lost letter that led {X_nameDef}'s family to its buried silver, and was given half.
[repaid] The colony sent on a lost note of credit, and {X_nameDef} sent back a share.
[joined] {X_nameDef} came to thank the colony for a lost letter, and stayed.
[dug] The colony read a lost letter and dug up the silver it described for itself.
[cashed] The colony cashed a lost note of credit meant for someone else.
[burned] The colony burned a satchel of lost letters.
[lost] The colony sent on a satchel of lost letters, and no answer came.

texts.li: [love] "I'll wait for your answer at the fair. If you don't come, I'll know." It's signed with an initial, and it's a proposal of marriage, to {X_nameDef} at {PLACE}. The rest of the letters are prices and weather and a dog that died.\n\n{X_nameDef} never got it. Whoever wrote it must have taken the silence for a no.

[cache] "Under the split tree by the east field, two spades down." One of the letters, to {X_nameDef} at {PLACE}, is from a father writing as his family fled their farm: the household silver is buried there, about {COUNT} of it, to be dug up when it's safe.\n\nThe farm is a day's walk from the colony. The letter never arrived.

[credit] Pay the bearer {COUNT} silver. The note is signed by a merchant house that still trades at {PLACE}, folded into a letter to {X_nameDef}, and made out to whoever carries it.\n\nIt was meant to settle a debt owed to {X_nameDef}'s family. It would settle one for anybody.

li.label: Send them all on, with a note saying how they were found
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} writes a short note to go with the satchel, explaining where it was found and that the seals were opened here. The letters go out with the next trader.

li.label: Act on it ourselves
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} takes the letter and goes to see to it.

outcomes.li: [love] {A_nameDef} sits up half the night writing a letter of {A_possessive} own to go with the old one, telling {X_nameDef} how it was found and how long it had waited. Both go out with the first rider to {PLACE}.
[cache] {A_nameDef} takes a spade and the letter, and sets off for the split tree by the east field.
[credit] The note goes to {PLACE} with the next trader, to be cashed for the colony.

li.label: Burn them all
li.outcome: The letters go into the stove, and the ashes are stirred until there's nothing left to read.

texts.li: [love] The old letter is still in {X_nameDef}'s hand. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has carried it all the way from {PLACE}: a proposal, written years ago by someone {X_nameDef} thought had forgotten {X_objective}. {X_nameDef} married someone else in the end, and buried them, and has come to see where the letter was found.

[love,personal] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came to the gate holding two letters: the old one, and the one {A_nameDef} wrote to go with it. {X_nameDef} wanted to meet whoever cared enough to write, and to see the road where the letter lay all those years.

[cache] Exactly where the letter said: under the split tree, two spades down. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} dug the family silver up last week, and has come from {PLACE} to thank the colony for sending the letter on. It was {X_possessive} father's, written as the family fled.
[credit] Paid at last, after years: the note of credit the colony sent on was honored at {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come all that way to say thank you in person.

[read] "If they hadn't been opened, they might have been thrown away." {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come from {PLACE} with the colony's note in hand, the one that owned up to the broken seals, and doesn't mind about them at all.

li.label: Welcome {X_objective}, and listen
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sat at the colony's table until late, telling {A_nameDef} who the letters were from and what had happened to everyone in them.

outcomes.li: [love] {X_nameDef} talked about the fair where the answer should have been given, and the summer after it, and laughed more than {A_nameDef} expected.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} looks round the room once, slowly, and asks where to put {X_possessive} things.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} is touched, and says no. There are people at {PLACE} who need {X_objective}.

texts.li: [lowtech] A pouch of seeds hangs at {X_nameDef}'s neck on a cord, and the first thing {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked at the gate was for the colony's best grower. The seeds come from a valley beyond the mountains, where the plant they grow into is nearly gone. They need good soil and someone patient.\n\n{X_nameDef} can't stay to grow them. {A_nameDef} has already looked at them three times.

[industrial] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} carries a tin of seeds from a farm that burned, the last of a kind {X_possessive} family grew for a hundred years. {X_nameDef} is leaving a few with every settlement that will plant them, so the kind isn't lost, and asks whether the colony will.\n\n{A_nameDef}, the colony's best grower, is already turning one over in {A_possessive} fingers.

[spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} carries a sealed case of seeds from a vault on a world that died. The plant they grow into is gone everywhere else. {X_nameDef} is going from colony to colony, leaving a few with anyone who'll plant them, and asks whether this one will.\n\n{A_nameDef}, the colony's best grower, is reading the label on the case very carefully.

"Who grows things here?" {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked at the gate, holding up a small bag of seeds. They're the last of a plant nearly lost, {X_nameDef} says, and they need a new home. {A_nameDef} has said yes twice already, before the council has said anything.

li.label: Plant them, and let {A_nameDef} tend them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} chooses the best patch of soil in the colony, plants the seeds with {X_nameDef} watching, and puts a little fence round them.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} plants the seeds at dusk, the way {X_nameDef} says it should be done, with a pinch of ash in each hole and a word over them.

li.label: Plant them somewhere out of the way
li.outcome: The seeds go into a corner by the fence where they won't be in anyone's way. {X_nameDef} looks at the spot for a long moment and says nothing.

li.label: Thank {X_objective}, but no
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} puts the pouch away and moves on in the morning, to find someone else.

coming.li: [seedssprout,tended] The stranger's seeds are in the ground, with {A_nameDef} watching over them. They should be up within {DAYS}.
[seedssprout,careless] The stranger's seeds are in the ground by the fence. Something should come up within {DAYS}.
[seedsreturn] {X_nameDef} said {X_pronoun} would come back to see what grew. Expected within {DAYS}.

remembered.li: [lost] The plant from the stranger's seeds still grows at the colony. {X_nameDef} never came back for it.
[lost] Every spring the stranger's plant comes up again at the colony, and {X_nameDef} still hasn't come to see it.

endings.li: [harvest,thrive] {X_nameDef} stood in the middle of the patch with a hand on each plant, and didn't say anything for a long time. Then {X_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} how to save the seed and helped bring in the first harvest. A gift came for the colony after {X_nameDef} had gone: {ITEM}.\n\nThe plant has a home now.

[harvest,rare] {X_nameDef} came back to find the blue bells in full flower and the whole yard smelling of them, and took a few seeds for the road. A parting gift for the colony followed: {ITEM}.\n\nTraders still stop at the gate to ask what that smell is.

[harvest] {X_nameDef} came back, saw what had grown, and helped {A_nameDef} bring in the first harvest of it before going on with seed for the next colony on the road. Something came afterward, for the colony's trouble: {ITEM}.
[joined] {X_nameDef} came back to see the garden and never left. {X_nameDef} sleeps in the colony now, and spends every morning in the patch with {A_nameDef}, arguing about water.

[passedon] {X_nameDef} left with a pouch of seed from the colony's own plants, to carry to the next settlement on the road. {FACTION} have heard about it, and so has everyone {X_nameDef} meets.\n\nA gift came back for the colony's trouble: {ITEM}.
[sold,rare] The cuttings sold almost as fast as {A_nameDef} could take them: {ITEM} silver in all, from traders who'd smelled the flowers from the road. The plant is in a dozen gardens now.
[sold] The colony sold cuttings to anyone who'd pay, and made {ITEM} silver. The plant grows in a few gardens along the road now.

[spread] The cuttings sold well, {ITEM} silver's worth, and then the plant got loose in the neighbors' fields. {FACTION} have been digging out its runners for a week, and they know where it came from.

[overgrown] The plant from the stranger's seeds has taken over a whole corner of the colony's fields, runners and all, and nothing else will grow there now. {A_nameDef} has stopped going near it.\n\nIt will have to be burned out, sooner or later.
[cleared] {A_nameDef} pulled the plant up by its runners, every one, and burned the lot. The field is clean again. {A_nameDef} kept one seed in a jar on the shelf, and won't say why.
[pulled] The plant from the stranger's seeds is gone, pulled up and composted. {A_nameDef} took it badly, and has been short with people all day.
[declined] {X_nameDef} went on with the seeds, to look for someone else to plant them. {A_nameDef} watched {X_objective} go from the field's edge.

[lost] {X_nameDef} never came back to see the garden, and the traders on the road haven't seen {X_objective} since. The plant grows on without {X_objective}, and {A_nameDef} saves its seed every year.

summaries.li: [harvest] The colony grew a stranger's rare seeds, and shared the first harvest with {X_nameDef}.
[joined] {X_nameDef} came back to see the garden grown from the stranger's seeds, and stayed.
[passedon] The colony grew a stranger's seeds and sent seed on with {X_nameDef} to the next settlement.
[sold] The colony sold cuttings of a rare plant grown from a stranger's seeds.
[spread] Cuttings the colony sold got loose in {FACTION}'s fields.
[overgrown] A stranger's seeds grew into a weed that choked part of the colony's fields.
[cleared] The colony burned out a weed grown from a stranger's seeds.
[pulled] The colony pulled up a plant grown from a stranger's seeds.
[declined] The colony turned down a stranger's rare seeds.
[lost] A stranger's seeds grew at the colony, and the stranger never came back.

texts.li: [thrive,tended] The stranger's seeds have come up in the patch {A_nameDef} gave them, and they're growing faster than anything else in the fields: broad leaves, a thick stem, and pods setting already. {A_nameDef} checks on them morning and evening, and has started talking to them.

[thrive,careless] Out by the fence, where the watering cans never go, the stranger's seeds have come up anyway, broad-leaved and strong and already setting pods. {A_nameDef} found them yesterday and has been carrying water out there ever since.

[weed] The stranger's seeds came up, and kept coming. The plant spreads by runners under the ground, and it has crept out of its patch into the next bed, and the one after that. {A_nameDef} pulled a runner up yesterday and found three more by evening.

[rare] The stranger's seeds have flowered: tall stalks with pale blue bells that smell of honey and smoke. A trader passing on the road stopped at the smell, asked what they were, and then asked what the colony would take for a cutting.

li.label: Let it grow
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} lets the plant be, and waters it.

outcomes.li: [weed] {A_nameDef} lets the plant be. It doesn't need the water, and it doesn't need the encouragement.

li.label: Pull it all up
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gets out the fork and starts digging.

li.label: Sell cuttings to anyone who'll pay
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} puts out a sign at the gate. Cuttings, for silver.

texts.li: [thrive] Thinner than before, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come back up the road to see what became of the seeds. {A_nameDef} took {X_objective} straight out to the patch, where the plants stand waist-high and heavy with pods.\n\n{X_nameDef} hasn't said a word yet.

[rare] The smell reached the road first. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came the last mile at a run, and is standing now among the blue bells, with the bees all round and both hands over {X_possessive} mouth.
As promised, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come back to see the garden. The plants are thriving, {A_nameDef} is proud of them, and {X_nameDef} wants to hear everything.

li.label: Show {X_objective} the garden, and share the harvest
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walked {X_nameDef} round every plant, and they brought in the first of the harvest together.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay and tend it
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} looked at the plants, and at {A_nameDef}, and said yes.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} is tempted, and says no. There are more seeds in the pouch, and more places that need them.

li.label: Give {X_objective} seed for the next colony
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} fills a pouch with seed from the colony's own plants, and {X_nameDef} ties it beside the old one.

texts.li: [lowtech] The troupe {X_nameDef} writes for plays from village to village, and on the road {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard enough about the colony to want to write a play about it. {X_nameDef} would like to stay a day, ask questions, and listen to whoever will talk.\n\nThe troupe will play it first at {PLACE}, and then wherever the road goes.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a playwright with a traveling company of {FACTION}, has arrived with a notebook and a very direct manner. The company wants a new play for the season, and {X_nameDef} wants it to be about the colony: the founding, the hard years, the people.\n\n{X_nameDef} asks for a day of the colony's time and its stories, and promises to be fair.

[colony:Merciful] Takes in strangers, forgives its enemies: that's what they say about the colony on the road, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who writes plays for a traveling troupe, doesn't believe a word of it. {X_nameDef} has come to see for {X_objective}self, and to write it all down.

[colony:Harsh] The things they say about the colony on the road are hard ones, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who writes for a traveling troupe, has heard most of them. {X_nameDef} would like the colony's side, for a play the troupe means to stage at {PLACE}.

[colony:Hardworking] "They say you work from dark to dark and never rest," {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} said at the gate. "That's a play." {X_nameDef} writes for a traveling troupe, and would like a day to ask questions.

li.label: Tell {X_objective} everything, good and bad
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat with {X_nameDef} until late and told the colony's story without leaving anything out. {X_nameDef} filled a notebook and started another.

li.label: Tell {X_objective} the best of it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} the colony's story, with the best parts first and the worst parts left out. {X_nameDef} wrote it all down and looked as if {X_pronoun} knew.

li.label: We'd rather not be in a play
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} puts the notebook away and leaves in the morning, still thinking.

coming.li: [playpremiere] {X_nameDef} is writing the play about the colony. The troupe means to bring it here first, within {DAYS}.
[playfans] The play about the colony is on the road. Word of how it goes should come within {DAYS}.
[famous|scandal|flop] The play about the colony opens at {PLACE} soon. Word of how it went should come within {DAYS}.
[refused] {X_nameDef} is writing the play about the colony anyway, from what {X_pronoun} heard on the road. It opens at {PLACE} within {DAYS}.

endings.li: [famous,honest] Audiences cry at the right moments, the troupe says. The play about the colony has been a hit at {PLACE} and in every town since, hard parts and all, and travelers who come by now ask which one is {A_nameDef}.
[famous,flattering] Brave colonists, wise councils, very little mud. The play has been a hit, and people along the road know the colony's name now. Some of them believe the play.
[famous,changed] The play opened at {PLACE} with the new ending the colony asked for, and it has been packing houses ever since. The neighbors talk about the colony as if they'd been there.
[famous,colony:Merciful] The troupe says audiences stand up for the best scene, the one where the colony takes in a stranger no one else would. The play has been a hit all along the road.
[famous,colony:Harsh] Hard, but fair: that's how the colony comes across on the stage, and the play has been a hit. The neighbors seem to respect the colony more for it.
[famous] The play about the colony has been a hit at {PLACE} and in every town the troupe has played since. The neighbors know the colony's name now.

[fanjoined] The admirer who walked here after seeing the play didn't leave. The colony is less heroic up close than it was on stage, the newcomer admits, and better for it.\n\nThe play is still drawing crowds at {PLACE}.

[scandal,honest] {X_nameDef} told the hard parts the way {A_nameDef} told them, and at {PLACE} some people didn't want to hear them. The play caused a scandal on its first night, and there have been arguments in the market since about whether the colony is good or not.
[scandal] At {PLACE} the play opened to a scandal. It shows the colony's worst choices, played big, with a villain who looks a lot like {A_nameDef}, and the neighbors are talking.

[flop] The play about the colony opened at {PLACE} and closed three nights later. The audience laughed in the wrong places, the set fell over, and the actor playing {A_nameDef} forgot all of {A_possessive} lines.\n\nThe troupe has gone back to an old favorite.
[refused,hit] {X_nameDef} wrote the play anyway, from rumors and tavern talk, and it's been a hit. Most of it is wrong. The neighbors like the colony more for it all the same.
[refused,flop] {X_nameDef} wrote the play anyway, from what {X_pronoun} heard on the road, and it closed after two nights. The colony is spared its moment on the stage.
[refused,scandal] {X_nameDef} wrote the play anyway, from the worst rumors on the road. The colony comes off badly in it, with no one there to set it straight.
[vanished] Nothing more was heard of {X_nameDef} or the play. A trader thought the troupe might have gone south for the winter, or broken up, or both.

summaries.li: [famous] A play about the colony was a hit along the road.
[fanjoined] An admirer of the play about the colony came to see it and stayed.
[scandal] A play about the colony caused a scandal at {PLACE}.
[flop] A play about the colony closed after three nights.
[refused] {X_nameDef} wrote a play about the colony without its help.
[vanished] A play about the colony was never staged.

titles.li: The play comes to the colony

texts.li: A cart of painted flats is standing at the gate. {X_nameDef} has brought the troupe back to play the colony's story to the colony first, before taking it on the road, and looks nervous about it. There's a part in it for {A_nameDef}, played by an actor taller and better-looking than {A_nameDef}.

[honest] "It's all in there," {X_nameDef} warns the council. "The good and the bad, just the way {A_nameDef} told it." The troupe is back to perform the play about the colony here first, before it goes on the road.

[flattering] {X_nameDef} has brought the troupe back to perform the play about the colony here first. From the rehearsal everyone could hear through the walls last night, the colony is very brave, and there's a lot of singing.

li.label: Watch it with everyone
li.outcome: The whole yard turned out for the play. People laughed at their own lines, argued about their own scenes, and cheered at the end.

outcomes.li: [honest] The colony watched its own story played out, the bad parts too, and was very quiet at the end. Then {A_nameDef} started clapping, and everyone joined in.

li.label: Have our best talker ask them to change the ending
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} took {X_nameDef} aside before the curtain and talked for an hour. The ending is different now, and better.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} took {X_nameDef} aside before the curtain. {X_nameDef} listened politely, and played the ending exactly as written.

li.label: Ask them not to play it here
li.outcome: The troupe packs up the flats again without unloading them, and takes the play straight to {PLACE}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} saw the play about the colony at {PLACE}, and walked for three days to see the real thing. {X_nameDef} has already asked which one is {A_nameDef}, and seems faintly disappointed that {A_nameDef} is shorter than the actor.
[changed] The new ending brought {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} all the way from {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} saw the play there and has come to find out whether any of it is true, the ending most of all.
[winter] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came through the snow to the colony's gate having seen the play at {PLACE}, and would like to shake {A_nameDef}'s hand. Then, perhaps, to stay a while.

li.label: Show {X_objective} around
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} showed {X_nameDef} the colony, the real one, mud and all. {X_nameDef} was delighted by every bit of it.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} said yes before {A_nameDef} had finished asking.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} was flattered, and said no. The colony is better as a story, {X_nameDef} thinks, than as a place to live.
